title: Microseasonal Capacity & Price-Shock Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for handling short-duration (1–6 week) demand uplifts driven by seasonal customer events, marketing campaigns, or external spikes that we classify as "microseasonal". The goal is to align headcount contingency, pricing levers, and capacity-sourcing so treasury and ops can react within 72 hours while protecting margin and SLAs.

Scope and definitions:
- Microseasonal uplift: demand increase of 20%–400% above baseline for 7–42 days with rapid onset (24–72h).
- Price-shock: pricing compression / spot-cost spike for GPU capacity or model serving that increases marginal cost per 1M tokens by >= 25% for >=72 hours.
- Skeleton hiring (shelf FTEs): small pool of pre-vetted contractors / temporary hires who can be converted to full-time or engaged for surge capacity.

High-level playbook summary (fast path):
1) T-72h alert: product/BD notifies finance + SRE via FIN-ALERT channel with expected demand window and risk score.
2) Finance ops triage: run quick sensitivity (sheet) for token demand vs unit-cost delta, produce three actions: (A) accept demand (clear to execute), (B) price-tilt + throttles, (C) defer non-critical traffic.
3) Immediate mitigations (within 6h): toggle per-route rate limits, enable model-fallback routes, enable prefix-KV cache boost for heavy routes, and send updated pricing signals to customers (temporary surcharge or credit-based quota).
4) Capacity hedge (24–72h): spin up reserved cloud burst (contracted soft-reserve), engage shelf contractors for SRE/ops, or reroute low-priority requests to cheaper quantized variants.
5) Post-mortem and billing reconciliation: measure delta margin, reconcile customer credits, and update runbook.

Decision matrices (quick reference) – token economics examples (illustrative):
- Baseline: 1M tokens served costs $6.40 (infrastructure + amortized infra ops).
- Microseasonal scenario A (50% uplift, spot GPU price +30%): marginal cost ~ $8.32 per 1M tokens.
- Microseasonal scenario B (200% uplift, spot GPU price +60%): marginal cost ~ $10.24 per 1M tokens.

Trigger thresholds (finance):
- If expected incremental spend > $25k/day AND margin on incremental tokens < 10% -> require exec approval (Head of Revenue + CFO).
- If incremental spend between $8k–$25k/day -> apply automated pricing tilt (5%–20%) + notify customers.
- < $8k/day -> absorb within ops buffer; run standard burst policy.

Headcount contingency plans (skeleton & surge):
- Shelf pool targets: 8 engineers (SRE/Inference), 2 infra devs (GPU ops), 2 finance analysts, 1 account rep. These are maintained as pre-approved contractors in vendor portal.
- Conversion rules: >21 days continuous surge -> convert up to 50% of shelf pool to full-time or extended term contractors.
- On-call rotas: temporarily extend SRE shifts by 1.5x (compensated) vs hiring; preferred for <10 day events.

Sourcing hierarchy (cost / lead time):
1) Quantized / cheaper model variants (immediate, low cost but quality tradeoff).
2) Reserved cloud burst (24–48h spin) via preferred partners (lower marginal latency risk).
3) Spot GPU bursts (immediate if market available, higher cost volatility).
4) On-prem / private customer-dedicated fallback (slowest, operational coordination needed).

Pricing levers and customer-facing options:
- Temporary surcharge (volume-weighted): per-customer, visible on billing dashboard; applied only if explicit notice given 24h prior OR urgent event with documented opt-out window.
- Credit-based quota top-up: allow customers to purchase microseasonal credits at a premium (e.g., 1.25x) to guarantee capacity.
- Route-level throttles / quality-tiering: downgrade to quantized model for non-latency-critical routes.
- Auto-fallback contract clause: for enterprise customers, enable pre-agreed fallback with reduced SLA and reduced unit price for non-critical traffic.

Quick sensitivity sheet (text table representation – for triage):
Columns: scenario | expected incremental tokens/day | incremental cost/day | surcharge needed to maintain 20% margin | recommended action
- Scenario 1 | +25M tokens | $160k | 12% | offer credits + enable cache
- Scenario 2 | +8M tokens | $51k | 8% | absorb inside buffer + throttle low-priority
- Scenario 3 | +3M tokens | $19k | 0% | absorb, monitor, no customer notice

Notes on model mix and sequence-length effects:
- Short-chat traffic (avg seq 75 tokens) benefits from batching; cost per token lower during busy spikes.
- Long-form generation (avg seq >1200 tokens) is disproportionately expensive — prioritize strict QoS for these during microseasonal events.
- Recommend per-route sequence-length caps during surge for non-committed tiers.

Operational runbook snippets (actionable checklist):
- Step 0: Confirm demand graph and expected window; create FIN-<date>-MICROSEASONAL ticket and tag relevant stakeholders.
- Step 1 (0–6h): Toggle route-level rate limits; enable KV cache warmup for top 10 routes; update alert thresholds for latency/error rates.
- Step 2 (6–24h): Open market for reserved burst capacity; contact broker on standby; push customer notices where required.
- Step 3 (24–72h): Engage shelf contractors; provision additional reserved pools; start daily finance reconciliation of incremental spend.
- Step 4 (post-event): Complete full margin analysis, customer credit reconciliation, and update the playbook with lessons.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Over-noticing customers causes churn. Mitigation: Default to opt-in surcharge and credits; require explicit customer opt-out for forced throttles on committed contracts.
- Risk: Spot market price inversion (cost spikes but capacity exists). Mitigation: Use soft-reserve contracts and early-market hedges based on forecast confidence score.
- Risk: Siloed ops decisions cause hidden costs. Mitigation: All surge actions require FIN ticket and daily shadow P&L posted to FIN channel.

Financial templates (links to sheets):
- Live triage spreadsheet: (placeholder) https://sheets.redwood.ai/spreadsheets/d/triage-microseasonal
- Cost-reconciliation workbook: (placeholder) https://sheets.redwood.ai/spreadsheets/d/cost-recon

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Define exact surge compensation policy for contractors vs FTE conversion thresholds (Sana to draft formal doc by 2026-11-10).
- Decide guardrail percent for pre-approved surcharge without exec sign-off (current recommendation: 12% max).
- Validate spot vs reserved burst latency profiles across regions (Ethan to collect 10-day sample by next sprint).
- Add legal-approved contract language for ephemeral surcharge and credits with minimal churn risk (Renee to loop in Legal).

Appendix: short worked example (7-day marketing blitz):
- Baseline tokens/day: 40M. Expected uplift: +150% -> 100M/day.
- Baseline cost/day: 40 * $6.40 = $256k.
- Uplift incremental tokens: 60M -> incremental cost at +30% spot = 60 * $8.32 = $499.2k.
- Incremental margin target 20% -> required surcharge on incremental tokens = approx 25% (round up to 30% to cover credit refunds/ops slippage).
- Recommended action: offer customers credit top-ups at 1.3x price, enable cache and model fallback for non-critical routes, spin reserved burst for critical enterprise routes.

This doc intentionally mixes high-level policy and quick triage artifacts so finance + ops can run a play quickly. The triage spreadsheet contains the numerical engine used for fast approvals. Keep this doc lean and link to the canonical live sheets.
